Strait of Hormuz Status: October 8, 2026 | Straits Daily Brief
Skip to content Straits Hormuz Live Monitor Day  221 Open? Live map News About Method API Live

Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
8 October 2026 .
Brent $ 102.61 + 1.18 % · Transits 4 (2026-10-04) · AI-assisted
01 Reuters reports Hormuz transits have fallen to their lowest level in over two months following recent attacks.

02 An IRGC adviser says the strait stays closed until Iran's demands are met; US CentCom rejects the closure claim, citing 20 million barrels of crude moving through.

03 Brent crude stood at $102.61 as of 05:57 UTC, up 1.18% over 24 hours, while IMF PortWatch recorded 4 transits on October 4, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz is registering its lowest transit volumes in more than two months, Reuters and The Hindu report, as attacks on shipping continue to suppress commercial movement through the waterway. The transit picture remains physically contested: an IRGC adviser, per Reuters, says the strait will remain closed until Iran's demands are met and that routes Iran deems illegal will soon be blocked, while US Central Command rejects the closure claim and says 20 million barrels of crude are moving through. IMF PortWatch recorded 4 transits on October 4, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day. Brent crude stood at $102.61 as of 05:57 UTC, a 24-hour gain of 1.18%, with WTI at $90.28. On the tanker incident front, the Panama-flagged On Peace, first reported struck on October 6 off Oman, sustained an engine-room fire and 12 crew members were injured, India's foreign ministry said, per MarineLink. Iran's Foreign Ministry, per Mehr News, Tehran state media, says conditions for ending the war and a Hormuz security deal with Oman have been set out, though Mehr News is state media and the claim should be treated as such. Fifty-three events have been indexed in the last 24 hours. As of 05:50 UTC, 130 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, flat over 24 hours, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the elevated band, flat over 24 hours, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
